item.title: Hikikomori: Re: Hikikomori
item.content:encoded:
The original idea was simple, but then I need some mechanics to make it happen. The "transport to another reality" bit was inspired by these two images:

https://i.ytimg.com/vi/LdCWEWzcedw/hqdefault.jpg
https://i.imgur.com/FG7oz2s.jpg

The sci-fi begins with the question: what if this actually worked? Or better, it seemed to work initially, but was reversed?

Suicide because I need some way to express that utter desperation that a hikikomori might feel, and also to set the tone. However, I don't want to use these specific pictures because of copyright reasons, and I have no need to involve any specific outside lore.

The similarity to Freddy Krueger or any other pop culture is coincidental. Freddy Krueger is a villain, the protagonist here is a essentially a victim, or thrown about by events like the protagonist in the film "12 Monkeys". I realized I might have to edit the draft to underline this point.

The anomaly is exhibited with self-imposed isolation because it needs an altered state of mind not available otherwise.

item.title: Irish Fairies: Re: Irish Fairies
item.content:encoded:
First of all, thanks for the crit. Secondly, multiple exploration logs/action scenarios would definitely work with the article, so I'll make sure to add that into the edit. One way I could structure it was this initial exploration log that reveals at least part of the SCP, a drone log that reveals the SCP's agency and malevolence, and a final action scenario that somehow contains the SCP (whether it be through neutralizing it or making a deal with it).

My main idea with the 'festival' was that the fairies have some sort of once in a millennium celebration that requires large amounts of humans to perform. I'm still deciding what exactly the festival's purpose is, but it's definitely not benevolent. Some of the ideas are a coronation of some monarch, a revival of some great being, or a way to connect two dimensions together. Again, those are just some of my ideas.

item.title: Irish Fairies: Re: Irish Fairies
item.content:encoded:
First of all, thanks for the crit, now let me explain some of my thought process

With the symmetrical hole, I really included that as a way for the Foundation to know something was off (rather than just a non-anomalous entity making people disappear), but you're right that I should tie it in at the end. I was mostly thinking of having actual fairies manipulate the situation rather than just fairy-like, so I could have a central fairy that speaks and talks to possibly one of MTF to show that it isn't just the forest being anomalous, but it's inhabitants. I also prefer having it be fairies rather than a fairy-like forest because it gives the SCP more agency rather than just 'spooky forest make bad things happen'.

A tale could work, to be honest, I was more biased towards an article because I'm more familiar with them compared to tales but I'll keep it in mind.

item.title: Love at Long Last: Love at Long Last
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): existential/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional):

  • Credentials Required
  • Object Description (yellow universe)
  • Object Description (red universe)
  • A series of messages between two Foundation personnel from parallel universes, (yellow universe)
  • A series of messages between two Foundation personnel from parallel universes (Red universe)
  • Event Log: Gothic Storm: First known RMK-Class Scenario for both parallel worlds (Yellow universe)
  • Event Log: Gothic Storm: First known RMK-Class Scenario for both parallel worlds (Red universe)

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block


The object is a pair of particles in between two separate branching worlds that allow for the communication between these two timelines via the transmission of information (possibly through Morse Code). A researcher by the name of Dr. Underwood attempts to contact her recently-deceased husband's counterpart in the alternate timeline, in a world where she had died rather than him during a similar event (possibly a containment breach, as both had worked together at the foundation when alive). The article contains a record of these messages, as well as documentation of cataclysmic events that transpired as a result of Dr. Underwood's attempts to reconnect with her husband.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

Dr. Underwood's husband had recently died two years prior due to a freak accident. Underwood isolates herself to focus on her work, and makes a breakthrough in inter-dimensional communication, where she comes into contact with Dr. Chase, her husband's counterpart in another dimension. In their communication, Chase reveals that Underwood had been the one to pass in his dimension, rather than him. As they talk, massive differences between the two worlds become evident, the primary one being that Chase's universe orbits a Red Dwarf while Underwood's earth (our Earth) orbits a Yellow dwarf. Eventually, the two realize that their communication is causing their realities to bleed into one another. Chase attempts to sever their connection to keep the two worlds separate, but Underwood continues to message him. This causes both particles to combine, accelerate the fusion process between both worlds. This leads to an event known as "Gothic Storm", the first known Reality-Merging Class Scenario (RMK-Class) in that reality. The aftermath is chaotic, and leads to public awareness of the Foundation, the release of numerous anomalies, and shifts of entire galaxies in the universe. Dr. Underwood had seemingly disappeared, while Dr. Chase was discovered in her office. The document ends with an interview with Chase, and remains the only documentation of this event

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The concept of an RMK-Class Scenario hasn't been used much on the wiki before. Additionally, it (attempts to) question the ethics of sacrificing the whole for personal gain. It attempts to paint the characters as both selfish and stingy, as well as human and sympathetic. I will admit that the concept itself isn't the most original, but the story and its consequences certainly are.

Additional Notes: This isn't my original story: I received the idea from this youtube video, and tried to make a unique ending: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K3W61Ae0M9g

item.title: My first SCP; The Corn Monkeys: Re: My first SCP; The Corn Monkeys
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Central Narrative

So really what I am looking for in this section is more of an overview of the article: what's the narrative being included? What do you do with this SCP beyond just describing all the parts? Like how are you really going to show the horror of this in a way that actually scares a reader? Are you having exploration logs or incident reports or what?

My big concern with this is that the idea is extremely complex: there's like, 8 different things that are going on here (the long teeth/claws, the spine as a tail to attract mates, can't leave the cornfield, die if fed the wrong thing etc) and it just…feels unnecessary? Like it makes this feel a lot more like an entry in a DnD Monster Manual than it does a short story about a scary monster, particularly since you don't actually have any kinda….indication of scenes involving said monster being scary, y'know?

Like, Alien or The Thing works because there's contrast: there's opening scenes setting up the characters, letting us know who they are and what they're like, followed by scenes in which they get glimpses of the monster and gradually like, get killed off and stuff, and then an ending where they resolve the tension of the monster somehow; and this feels like all it has is the monster? But a monster isn't scary in isolation: it's scary because of what it does and to who.

item.title: SCP Idea: The Necro-Matriarch Broadcast Manifestations: Re: SCP Idea: The Necro-Matriarch Broadcast Manifestations
item.content:encoded:
What is the reason in the Foundation universe world for the radio to do what it does? Did someone make it because they wanted to talk to their grandma? Is a ghost grandma living in the radiowaves to haunt them? Some other reason?

Oh yeah, here is what I am trying to imply in the story; a mysterious benevolent entity/company is trying to help humanity regain contact with their dead loved ones, in this case, grandmas. How? by turning previously non-anomalous radios into a medium of such conversations with said individuals, though it is still unsure whether they are the actual person.

My point is that this is a kind of boring initial investigation setup.

Okay, I respect your opinion. Though I still like to point out that some articles do have a similar setup as mine, which I took the inspiration from.

Why would the creator want to play games with the Foundation?

A part of the mystery I would also like to imply with the readers. Also, I planned this as an initial setup for future articles of mine.

I'm not familiar with antique radios. Although, if it only affects such radios, would there really be that many people who would be affected by such an anomaly, to the point where the Foundation would have enough cases to notice?

Yep.

I personally am not convinced you'd be able to make a tale for this—the material I've mentioned would make more sense for a log or supplement page. Focus on writing an SCP article first.

  • Oh yeah, that's the right word I am looking for. A tale in a format of what you've said, my bad.
  • Yeah, that's what I am planning to do first

item.title: The Unrune (For Greenlight): The Unrune (For Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP layout followed by information on where the object was recovered from and the groups connected with it. Possible addendums or test logs will tie in more of the important story

Elevator Pitch: A rune stone that defies physics, disobeys logic, and removes any sense of comfort. According to all attempts to gather data, it doesn't exist, yet we perceive it with our senses. However the rune engraved on it can only be seen, not felt, and in any image of the object it is blank.

Central Narrative: A cult worshipping the god of chaos believes this rune stone imprisons him and it is their duty to set him free once more. The GOC ended up with it, tried to destroy it and couldn't, and decided to give it to the foundation since containing is more their speed. The rune isn't what the cult thinks, but there's more to it than the foundation knows and it ties into a larger story relating to this so called god and his cult.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The object defies reality and physics and is tied to some god, but isn't really dangerous or powerful. It's more focused on the story I want to introduce but a reality defying object that doesn't do much and a god that isn't a god might be refreshing amongst the massive distortions and apocalyptic deities.

Additional Notes: This IS NOT meant to be some new all powerful, world ending, eldritch being. I don't want to make this about yet another god who wants to destroy humanity. I'm starting small, with this rune, so I don't come across like it's my goal to top anybody else or "have the baddest scp". Just want some cool ideas and a good story because that's what I personally love.

item.title: Greenlight: Healing SCP with potential for GK scenario: Re: Greenlight: Healing SCP with potential for GK scenario
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

The range of its search doubles every 4 hours that it doesn't have someone to heal and it gets more and more agitated that it can't find someone to heal.

How does this 'searching' work? Like is it physically going to places? Does it just, radar sweep for people? Why does the range increase exponentially like this?

After 24 hours it will attempt to heal terminal medical conditions, resulting in accidental euthanasia.

how does this result in accidental euthanasia? This feels like you're going for like 'too much healing is bad' or something but it's not exactly clear how it gets here since the implication is the mannequin is good at healing? This applies to the 'healed of humanity' angle too like…there's not really any indication the mannequin heals badly until it gets too big?

I think my big issue with this is that…it just, doesn't feel very interesting to me? There's a lot of elements that are here but don't really go anywhere, or just feel added in to add more threat to this (e.g., the 'gk world ending scenario' angle, the 'aggression' of the SCP, the exponentially increasing range), and it feels like focussing on this being a SCP that can heal as the only thing it does would be more effective, particularly since the core of the story you want to tell is 'foundation tries to stop it healing and it doesn't'.

Part of the problem with this though is it feels…very surface level? You don't really do anything with this beyond having it heal someone, and I'm just kinda…looking for more emotional impact here? Like, some kind of exploration of its existence that makes me feel sorry for it not helping, or like, really ties the 'overhealing' kinda stuff in so it feels like an important part of the narrative or something, y'know?

item.title: Abiogenesis SCP (Greenlight 1/2): Re: Abiogenesis (SCP)

I'm gonna greenlight this.

Thank you!

item.title: A narrative about the foundation censoring stuff again.: Re: A narrative about the foundation censoring stuff again.
item.content:encoded:
I guess at the end of the day, my big question here is: so what?

Like, there's a lot of cool intrigue here and like, deception and cool plans, but it all just kinda boils down to 'all SCP sites in the US are actually UIU sites' and it feels…underwhelming? Like I don't really have a clear idea of what the stakes of this are or how you're like, going to hint at this being the case without making it really obvious? And I'm not sure how this plan actually works: why does adding brainwashing to Foundation sites affect the UIU as a whole? Why does it cause the UIU sites to become effectively Foundation sites? Or do you mean the Foundation infiltrates every UIU site and adds brainwashing to them, and if so, how do they manage to do this? How do they manage to keep this under wraps?

I think to summarise, my concern here is that this feels like a really great start but it also feels like it's missing something that just, ties it all together and leaves a pit of dread in the readers stomach, y'know?

item.title: SCP Idea: The Necro-Matriarch Broadcast Manifestations: Re: SCP Idea: The Necro-Matriarch Broadcast Manifestations
item.content:encoded:
I think, at the core, my central issue with this is that not much actually like…happens over the course of the piece? Like, between the introduction and the ending, the only thing that actually changes is the foundation discovering more of these; and I'm left wanting more out of this.

It feels like you kinda have two conflicting angles here: the intimate, personal story about someone being affected by their grandma on the radio and like, reconnecting with them; and the much larger scope, much less personal one where the foundation has to deal with like, these being mass sold and the whole broken masquerade angle, and to me, the first just, feels a lot more interesting? It feels to me like the whole selling angle is just kinda there and doesn't really go anywhere because at the end of the day: if these are occasionally sold, what does that cause to happen? Why does it matter?

And so it seems to me that stripping this right down to it's core and focussing on the impact the radio has on e.g. a d-class and like, them like, reconnecting with their grandmother and forgiving her for her mistakes in life, and then, slowly, over time, them coming to the realisation this isn't their grandmother and having the whole forgiveness thing ripped away from them again and the old wounds reopened would be a lot more effective, narratively, than this? Or like…at least having some kind of personal, emotional growth story influenced by like, the radio, y'know?

item.title: The Chaos Insurgency is dead. Long live the Chaos Insurgency.: Re: The Chaos Insurgency is dead. Long live the Chaos Insurgency.
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

Also important to note that Corbenic isn't the organization…

I don't see the problem here? I have clearly distinguished between Corbenic (where most of the place happens) and the Three-Moons-Initiative a.k.a. United Nations Afterlives. So this one mention strikes me as odd?

Do you have some idea for actual characters that the reader can relate to (or be entertained by?) For example, characters with dimensions (not just nameless)

Now this one… I see your point, so let me elaborate:
As you have stated yourself, it is a detailed plot, e.g. no matter how short I keep it (and brevity isn't exactly my strength) it will have some length, and I am afraid that giving them to much time for "character development" and deeper insights into their emotions will just bloat the article, especially if they are throw-aways and never seen again.

This does not mean that I write rigid, featureless shells - most of the characterisation will come by the way they (inter)act. For example, I plan one of the surrenderers (is that a word?) to be an office clerk, and them explaining their backstory with the Insurgency ("Every evening I dumped a truckload of fish down the enclosure. I never asked what lived in there, but they paid me well for a simple feeding job."). It is the classical "show, don't tell" principle.

I guess what I want to make clear is that I tend to write plot-focused, not character focused. I don't want to steal the show of the storyline with "obnoxious OCs", to word it bluntly. I don't like getting overly invested into characters to the degree many people on this site display; thankfully, there is indeed a niche for my style.

I'd rather captivate with clever plots and atmospheric prose, which are more of my strengths.

Anyway, to much babbling about characterisation. Now, about your other thing about continuities:

Additionally, consider this: if COrbenic exists in the in-universe SCP-5000 does, then that's a new rash of humanity going to the next life once the Foundation kills everyone… as multiple alt reality Earths have arrived in Corbenic (that's where the triple moons came from) meaning Corbenic is not limited to one continua.

This is where it gets interesting, but also a matter of headcanon. I could go on about this for hours, but it would lead deeply into my own convoluted headcanon, and that is more suited for PMs (also, it requires lecture of some lengthy stuff I wrote on -DE, making everything worse).
In short, I see Corbenic as the garbage dump of the Second Hytoth where everything expulsed from the other universes (say, souls of the dead) eventually ends up there. I also tend to follow EdAWACSdenyY's interpretation of the Insurgency, Foundation and GOC as "three sides of the same coin", portraying the Insurgency as mislead party that anyway tries to further mankind. ("The road of hell is paved with good intentions" and so on.)

As the Initiative has indeed tried to stop evil Foundations in other universes in the past, but seems to do exactly nothing about the SCP-5000 Foundation, the outrage is definitely justified, and the multiversal Insurgency will certainly come to aid this endeavour, especially since the Initiative caving in would be a very interesting precedent for the future, something any Insurgency would be interested in.

Especially since they appear to follow a righteous cause, aren't they? If we are watched, loved, and protected, where are they?

I have chosen this setting explicitly with the multiple realities in mind, but I do not think it is an issue (if it is an issue at all) to tackle in the story, especially since every reader will have a different interpretation anyway, and by introducing Corbenic, I am already straining many people's headcanon more than enough.

item.title: Ms. G. Lass: Re: Ms. G. Lass
item.content:encoded:
I am well aware this isn't how glass works.

Right, sure, but my point is that it feels like "woman who bursts into fire" and "woman made of glass" are two things that like…aren't really tied together here? It feels like you could tell the entire story of this without the person being made of glass cos the focus is entirely on her bursting into fire.

I was actually going to have the article just give a passing glance at the recontainment procedures. My main focus was going to be the struggle of the pair of researchers. After successful containment, I could do some interview logs.

So like, what's the plan for these? My concern is that like…the struggle here is just gonna be fairly generically them talking about recontainment but?

That is very similar to SCP-706: The Perfect Porcelain Doll

In some ways? 706 is more about like…altering your body to be perfect; whereas my pitch is more 'preventing your body shattering so you don't die'.

This feels…exceedingly lolfoundation in style, possibly to the pieces detriment: like, it feels…really like it's leaning into all the worst traits of it in a way that doesn't quite vibe for me.

I think part of it is that the plot feels…not that interesting in general? It's just a generic 'mtf team goes in to clean up mess' style plot, and that's fine but since I don't really vibe with the lolfoundation aspects, I'm not really sure whether there'd be enough character for this to like…work for me?

item.title: Abiogenesis SCP (Greenlight 1/2): Re: Abiogenesis (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
I think your proposed changes could definitely help here (specifically the second last paragraph): it feels like this might really be lacking in tension without some kind of uncertainty about how it'll go, and that in turn requires the reader to know roughly what the ending is without knowing how they'll get there.

My, concern here is that it feels like this is kinda balancing on the knife edge between being really great and really boring with not a lot of margin for error if you don't nail the balance: like, to execute this well, you're really going to have to pull off an ambitious work blending characters and intrigue together in a way that'll be pretty challenging, and there's definitely the possibility that there's a huge section in the middle where not much happens; but I think as long as you manage to keep it tight and character focussed and really make it work, this could be good.

I'm gonna greenlight this.
